title: Chapter7
description: Finnish vocabulary: travel, transport, tickets, directions and verbs

questions.question: Timetable / Schedule
questions.explanation: 'Aikataulu' means timetable or schedule.
questions.exampletranslate: I check the train timetable.

questions.question: Discount
questions.explanation: 'Alennus' means discount; its genitive is 'alennuksen'.
questions.exampletranslate: You get a discount on the ticket.

questions.question: Value
questions.explanation: 'Arvo' means value.
questions.exampletranslate: The travel card's value is ten euros.

questions.question: Station
questions.explanation: 'Asema' means station.
questions.exampletranslate: The train leaves from the station.

questions.question: Machine / Vending machine
questions.explanation: 'Automaatti' means an automatic machine or vending machine; its genitive is 'automaatin'.
questions.exampletranslate: I buy the ticket from the machine.

questions.question: Gasoline / Petrol
questions.explanation: 'Bensa' means gasoline or petrol (informal).
questions.exampletranslate: The car needs petrol.

questions.question: Band (music group)
questions.explanation: 'Bändi' means a band (music group).
questions.exampletranslate: The band plays at the festival.

questions.question: Affordable
questions.explanation: 'Edullinen' means affordable or reasonably priced; its genitive is 'edullisen'.
questions.exampletranslate: This ticket is affordable.

questions.question: Pensioner
questions.explanation: 'Eläkeläinen' means pensioner or retiree; its genitive is 'eläkeläisen'.
questions.exampletranslate: A pensioner gets a discount.

questions.question: South
questions.explanation: 'Etelä' means south; its genitive is 'etelän'.
questions.exampletranslate: I travel south for the holiday.

questions.question: To scrub / rub
questions.explanation: 'Hangata' (type 4 verb) means to scrub or rub; 'hankaan' is 'I scrub'.
questions.exampletranslate: I scrub the floor with a brush.

questions.question: To practice
questions.explanation: 'Harjoitella' (type 3 verb) means to practice; 'harjoittelen' is 'I practice' (takes a partitive object).
questions.exampletranslate: I practice the Finnish language.

questions.question: Rarely
questions.explanation: 'Harvoin' means rarely.
questions.exampletranslate: I rarely travel by ship.

questions.question: Easy
questions.explanation: 'Helppo' means easy; its genitive is 'helpon'.
questions.exampletranslate: This course is easy.

questions.question: Slow
questions.explanation: 'Hidas' means slow; its genitive is 'hitaan'.
questions.exampletranslate: This train is slow.

questions.question: Wild / Fierce
questions.explanation: 'Hurja' means wild or fierce.
questions.exampletranslate: It was a wild trip.

questions.question: To announce / inform
questions.explanation: 'Ilmoittaa' (type 1 verb) means to announce or inform; 'ilmoitan' is 'I announce'.
questions.exampletranslate: I announce the departure time.

questions.question: Afternoon
questions.explanation: 'Iltapäivä' means afternoon.
questions.exampletranslate: The train leaves in the afternoon.

questions.question: East
questions.explanation: 'Itä' means east; its genitive is 'idän'.
questions.exampletranslate: The sun rises from the east.

questions.question: River
questions.explanation: 'Joki' means river; its genitive is 'joen'.
questions.exampletranslate: The river flows through the city.

questions.question: Santa Claus
questions.explanation: 'Joulupukki' means Santa Claus; its genitive is 'joulupukin'.
questions.exampletranslate: Santa Claus lives in Lapland.

questions.question: Exercise / Gym workout
questions.explanation: 'Jumppa' means exercise or a workout class; its genitive is 'jumpan'.
questions.exampletranslate: I go to exercise class once a week.

questions.question: Train
questions.explanation: 'Juna' means train.
questions.exampletranslate: I travel north by train.

questions.question: Train ticket
questions.explanation: 'Junalippu' means train ticket; its genitive is 'junalipun'.
questions.exampletranslate: I buy a train ticket to Helsinki.

questions.question: To organize
questions.explanation: 'Järjestää' (type 1 verb) means to organize or arrange; 'järjestän' is 'I organize'.
questions.exampletranslate: I organize a party on Saturday.

questions.question: To get off / stay
questions.explanation: 'Jäädä' (type 2 verb) means to stay or remain; 'jään pois' means 'I get off' (used with 'mistä').
questions.exampletranslate: I get off the bus in the centre.

questions.question: Calendar
questions.explanation: 'Kalenteri' means calendar.
questions.exampletranslate: I mark the trip in the calendar.

questions.question: Map
questions.explanation: 'Kartta' means map; its genitive is 'kartan'.
questions.exampletranslate: I check the route on the map.

questions.question: Far away (direction)
questions.explanation: 'Kauas' means (to) far away, used for direction (compare 'kaukana' for location).
questions.exampletranslate: I travel far away to the south.

questions.question: Season / Period
questions.explanation: 'Kausi' means season or period; its genitive is 'kauden'.
questions.exampletranslate: The summer season is busy.

questions.question: Single ticket
questions.explanation: 'Kertalippu' means a single (one-time) ticket; its genitive is 'kertalipun'.
questions.exampletranslate: I buy a single ticket for the bus.

questions.question: In the middle of
questions.explanation: 'Keskellä' means in the middle of (used with the genitive).
questions.exampletranslate: The tower is in the middle of the city.

questions.question: To interest
questions.explanation: 'Kiinnostaa' (type 1 verb) means to interest; 'minua kiinnostaa' means 'it interests me'.
questions.exampletranslate: Travel interests me.

questions.question: Sized (a certain size)
questions.explanation: 'Kokoinen' means '-sized' (of a certain size); its genitive is 'kokoisen'.
questions.exampletranslate: I need a bag of this size.

questions.question: Conductor (on a train)
questions.explanation: 'Konduktööri' means a train conductor.
questions.exampletranslate: The conductor checks the tickets.

questions.question: Rapids (in a river)
questions.explanation: 'Koski' means rapids in a river; its genitive is 'kosken'.
questions.exampletranslate: The boat goes down the rapids.

questions.question: To go / move / travel
questions.explanation: 'Kulkea' (type 1 verb) means to go, move or travel; 'kuljen' is 'I go/move'.
questions.exampletranslate: I travel to work by bus.

questions.question: Vehicle / Means of transport
questions.explanation: 'Kulkuneuvo' means a vehicle or means of transport.
questions.exampletranslate: The train is a fast means of transport.

questions.question: Course
questions.explanation: 'Kurssi' means course.
questions.exampletranslate: I attend a Finnish course.

questions.question: Village
questions.explanation: 'Kylä' means village.
questions.exampletranslate: I live in a small village.

questions.question: Ride / Lift
questions.explanation: 'Kyyti' means a ride or lift; its genitive is 'kyydin'.
questions.exampletranslate: Can I get a ride to the centre?

questions.question: Used (second-hand)
questions.explanation: 'Käytetty' means used or second-hand; its genitive is 'käytetyn'.
questions.exampletranslate: I buy a used car.

questions.question: To load / download / charge
questions.explanation: 'Ladata' (type 4 verb) means to load, download or charge; 'lataan' is 'I load/charge'.
questions.exampletranslate: I load (top up) the travel card.

questions.question: Ship
questions.explanation: 'Laiva' means ship.
questions.exampletranslate: I go to Stockholm by ship.

questions.question: Airport
questions.explanation: 'Lentokenttä' means airport; its genitive is 'lentokentän'.
questions.exampletranslate: The plane leaves from the airport.

questions.question: Airplane
questions.explanation: 'Lentokone' means airplane; its genitive is 'lentokoneen'.
questions.exampletranslate: The airplane lands soon.

questions.question: To fly
questions.explanation: 'Lentää' (type 1 verb) means to fly; 'lennän' is 'I fly'.
questions.exampletranslate: I fly to Lapland tomorrow.

questions.question: Castle
questions.explanation: 'Linna' means castle.
questions.exampletranslate: We visit the old castle.

questions.question: Ticket
questions.explanation: 'Lippu' means ticket; its genitive is 'lipun'.
questions.exampletranslate: I show the ticket to the conductor.

questions.question: Ticket sales
questions.explanation: 'Lipunmyynti' means ticket sales; its genitive is 'lipunmyynnin'.
questions.exampletranslate: The ticket sales are at the station.

questions.question: Departure
questions.explanation: 'Lähtö' means departure; its genitive is 'lähdön'.
questions.exampletranslate: The train's departure is at ten o'clock.

questions.question: West
questions.explanation: 'Länsi' means west; its genitive is 'lännen'.
questions.exampletranslate: The sun sets in the west.

questions.question: Travel card
questions.explanation: 'Matkakortti' means travel card; its genitive is 'matkakortin'.
questions.exampletranslate: I load money onto the travel card.

questions.question: Suitcase
questions.explanation: 'Matkalaukku' means suitcase; its genitive is 'matkalaukun'.
questions.exampletranslate: I pack the suitcase.

questions.question: Passenger
questions.explanation: 'Matkustaja' means passenger.
questions.exampletranslate: The passenger sits on the train.

questions.question: Outbound / One-way trip
questions.explanation: 'Meno' means the outbound or one-way trip; its genitive is 'menon'.
questions.exampletranslate: I buy only a one-way ticket.

questions.question: Return ticket (round trip)
questions.explanation: 'Menopaluu' means a return (round-trip) ticket, from 'meno' and 'paluu'.
questions.exampletranslate: I buy a return ticket to Tampere.

questions.question: Sea
questions.explanation: 'Meri' means sea; its genitive is 'meren'.
questions.exampletranslate: The ship travels on the sea.

questions.question: Hill
questions.explanation: 'Mäki' means hill; its genitive is 'mäen'.
questions.exampletranslate: The house is on top of the hill.

questions.question: To return
questions.explanation: 'Palata' (type 4 verb) means to return; 'palaan' is 'I return'.
questions.exampletranslate: I return home in the evening.

questions.question: Return (the act)
questions.explanation: 'Paluu' means the return or the journey back.
questions.exampletranslate: The return takes two hours.

questions.question: Service house / Assisted living
questions.explanation: 'Palvelutalo' means a service house or assisted-living home.
questions.exampletranslate: The elderly person lives in a service house.

questions.question: To put / place
questions.explanation: 'Panna' (type 3 verb) means to put or place; 'panen' is 'I put'.
questions.exampletranslate: I put the bag on the bench.

questions.question: Passport
questions.explanation: 'Passi' means passport.
questions.exampletranslate: I need a passport on the trip.

questions.question: To fear / be afraid
questions.explanation: 'Pelätä' (type 4 verb) means to fear; 'pelkään' is 'I fear' (takes a partitive object).
questions.exampletranslate: I am afraid of flying.

questions.question: At the destination
questions.explanation: 'Perillä' means at the destination (having arrived).
questions.exampletranslate: We will soon be at the destination.

questions.question: North
questions.explanation: 'Pohjoinen' means north; its genitive is 'pohjoisen'.
questions.exampletranslate: Lapland is in the north.

questions.question: Park
questions.explanation: 'Puisto' means park.
questions.exampletranslate: I walk in the park.

questions.question: Changing room / Dressing room
questions.explanation: 'Pukuhuone' means changing room or dressing room; its genitive is 'pukuhuoneen'.
questions.exampletranslate: I change clothes in the changing room.

questions.question: To be missing / lacking
questions.explanation: 'Puuttua' (type 1 verb) means to be missing or lacking; 'se puuttuu' means 'it is missing'.
questions.exampletranslate: One ticket is missing.

questions.question: To request / ask for
questions.explanation: 'Pyytää' (type 1 verb) means to request or ask for; 'pyydän' is 'I request'.
questions.exampletranslate: I ask for help on the trip.

questions.question: Capital city
questions.explanation: 'Pääkaupunki' means capital city; its genitive is 'pääkaupungin'.
questions.exampletranslate: Helsinki is the capital of Finland.

questions.question: To get to / be able to go
questions.explanation: 'Päästä' (type 2 verb) means to get to or be able to go; 'pääsen' is 'I get to'.
questions.exampletranslate: I get to the destination at five o'clock.

questions.question: Rail / Track
questions.explanation: 'Raide' means rail or track (e.g. a platform track); its genitive is 'raiteen'.
questions.exampletranslate: The train arrives at track two.

questions.question: Border
questions.explanation: 'Raja' means border.
questions.exampletranslate: We cross the border by train.

questions.question: Building
questions.explanation: 'Rakennus' means building; its genitive is 'rakennuksen'.
questions.exampletranslate: This is an old building.

questions.question: To build
questions.explanation: 'Rakentaa' (type 1 verb) means to build; 'rakennan' is 'I build'.
questions.exampletranslate: I build a new house.

questions.question: Beach / Shore
questions.explanation: 'Ranta' means beach or shore; its genitive is 'rannan'.
questions.exampletranslate: I walk on the beach.

questions.question: Railway station
questions.explanation: 'Rautatieasema' means railway station.
questions.exampletranslate: The train leaves from the railway station.

questions.question: Dining car
questions.explanation: 'Ravintolavaunu' means dining car (on a train).
questions.exampletranslate: I eat lunch in the dining car.

questions.question: Backpack
questions.explanation: 'Reppu' means backpack; its genitive is 'repun'.
questions.exampletranslate: I carry the backpack on my back.

questions.question: To arrive
questions.explanation: 'Saapua' (type 1 verb) means to arrive; 'saavun' is 'I arrive'.
questions.exampletranslate: The train arrives on time.

questions.question: Raincoat
questions.explanation: 'Sadetakki' means raincoat; its genitive is 'sadetakin'.
questions.exampletranslate: In the rain I wear a raincoat.

questions.question: Dictionary
questions.explanation: 'Sanakirja' means dictionary, from 'sana' (word) and 'kirja' (book).
questions.exampletranslate: I look up the word in the dictionary.

questions.question: Company / Club / Society
questions.explanation: 'Seura' means company, club or society.
questions.exampletranslate: I like good company.

questions.question: Inspection / Check
questions.explanation: 'Tarkastus' means inspection or check; its genitive is 'tarkastuksen'.
questions.exampletranslate: There is a ticket inspection on the train.

questions.question: To dance
questions.explanation: 'Tanssia' (type 1 verb) means to dance; 'tanssin' is 'I dance'.
questions.exampletranslate: I dance at the festival.

questions.question: Information / Knowledge
questions.explanation: 'Tieto' means information or knowledge; its genitive is 'tiedon'.
questions.exampletranslate: I want more information about the trip.

questions.question: To function / work / act
questions.explanation: 'Toimia' (type 1 verb) means to function, work or act; 'toimin' is 'I function/act'.
questions.exampletranslate: The machine does not work.

questions.question: Tower
questions.explanation: 'Torni' means tower.
questions.exampletranslate: We climb to the top of the tower.

questions.question: To come across / meet
questions.explanation: 'Tulla vastaan' means to come towards or come across (e.g. meet someone on the way).
questions.exampletranslate: A friend comes to meet me at the station.

questions.question: Full
questions.explanation: 'Täysi' means full; its genitive is 'täyden'.
questions.exampletranslate: The bus is full.

questions.question: Swimming pool (indoor)
questions.explanation: 'Uimahalli' means an indoor swimming pool.
questions.exampletranslate: I go swimming at the swimming pool.

questions.question: Ready / Finished
questions.explanation: 'Valmis' means ready or finished; its genitive is 'valmiin'.
questions.exampletranslate: I am ready for the trip.

questions.question: To compare
questions.explanation: 'Verrata' (type 4 verb) means to compare; 'vertaan' is 'I compare'.
questions.exampletranslate: I compare the ticket prices.

questions.question: 24-hour period (day and night)
questions.explanation: 'Vuorokausi' means a 24-hour period (a full day and night); its genitive is 'vuorokauden'.
questions.exampletranslate: The trip lasts one full day.
